components.name: Button
components.description: The single mechanism for triggering an action. Weight (primary → destructive) signals how much attention the action deserves.

components.name: Input
components.description: Text entry and search. Search fields in persistent chrome show a keyboard shortcut hint; form fields inside a flow do not.

components.name: Badge & counter
components.description: Counters show an unseen total in navigation; dots show state on a row; tag badges label a category.

components.name: List row
components.description: Any scannable list — inbox, transactions, notifications — where someone compares many items at a glance.

components.name: Empty state
components.description: Replaces a bare blank screen when a list has zero items — first run, cleared, or blocked.

components.name: Table
components.description: For rows with three or more comparable attributes — use the List row component instead when a row only really has a title and one piece of metadata.

components.name: Dropdown
components.description: Covers two Base UI primitives: a Menu for a set of actions attached to a trigger, and a Select for choosing one value from a fixed list.

components.name: Card
components.description: A bordered container for related content. Three uses: a plain grouping surface, a clickable summary, and a single-stat headline.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Two designs: primary tabs switch between full page-level views; secondary tabs switch a scoped region without changing the page.

components.name: Switch
components.description: An immediate, self-contained on/off setting — it takes effect the moment it's toggled, with no separate save step.

components.name: Checkbox & radio
components.description: Checkbox for zero-to-many selections; radio for exactly one choice from a small, fully visible set of options.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Progressive disclosure for secondary content the person doesn't need immediately — never the primary content on a screen.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: An interruption reserved for decisions that need a deliberate, in-the-moment answer — most often the confirming step a destructive Button already promises.

components.name: Toast
components.description: A brief, self-dismissing confirmation for something that already happened — a payout landing, an invoice getting paid.

components.name: Amount input
components.description: Money entry, specifically — distinct from the plain text Input because precision, asset, and available balance all have to be visible at once.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: Represents a person or business — a client, a team member, a merchant — anywhere the product needs a face rather than just a name.

components.name: Alert / banner
components.description: Page-level, persistent messaging — the pattern already used for the notes throughout this document. Different from a Toast because it doesn't go away on its own.

components.name: Command palette
components.description: What the ⌘K hint on the persistent Search field actually opens — search and act on anything in the product without leaving the keyboard.

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: A placeholder shaped exactly like the content it stands in for, while a balance, list, or chart is still loading.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: Required on every icon-only Button, per that component's own accessibility note — this is the piece that actually delivers it.

components.name: Pagination
components.description: Pairs with the Table component once a list is long enough to split across pages.

components.name: Chart (area)
components.description: The only chart type in this system for now. Reserved for a value trending over time — balance, volume, activity — where the filled region is what communicates magnitude, not for comparing unrelated categories.

components.name: Nav item
components.description: Primary navigation inside a workspace. Icon and label always travel together — never icon-only in this context.
